"AVATAR: THE FOUR ELEMENTS

Open-World RPG Adventure Game

Create a fully playable 3D open-world RPG inspired by the universe of Avatar: The Last Airbender.

The game takes place in a vast world inspired by the Four Nations: the Water Tribes, the Earth Kingdom, the Fire Nation, and the Air Nomads.

The player must be able to freely explore the world, discover villages, cities, temples, forests, mountains, oceans, caves, and ancient ruins.

1. Character Creation and Origins

At the beginning of the game, the player creates their own character.

Allow the player to customize:

- Name
- Gender
- Appearance
- Hairstyle and hair color
- Skin tone
- Clothing
- Starting nation
- Character background

The player must be born into one of the four nations.

Depending on their origin, they will have access to a different bending ability.

There are five possible character types:

- Waterbender
- Earthbender
- Firebender
- Airbender
- Avatar

The Avatar is extremely rare. If the player is born as the Avatar, they can eventually master all four elements.

If the player is not the Avatar, they can only master their native element.

2. Elemental Bending System

Create a dynamic elemental combat system with fluid animations and different abilities for each element.

Waterbending:

- Control water
- Create water whips
- Launch waves
- Freeze water into ice
- Create ice spikes
- Control large amounts of water
- Heal using waterbending

Earthbending:

- Raise walls and pillars
- Throw rocks at enemies
- Create earthquakes
- Open cracks in the ground
- Control large boulders
- Create stone armor

Firebending:

- Shoot fireballs
- Create fire streams
- Launch powerful explosions
- Perform fire kicks and punches
- Generate lightning (advanced ability)
- Redirect lightning (advanced ability)

Airbending:

- Create air blasts
- Generate powerful tornadoes
- Push enemies away
- Create air shields
- Glide using an air glider
- Perform aerial attacks

Each element must have its own skill tree, abilities, animations, and progression system.

3. Avatar System

If the player is born as the Avatar, they have a special progression system.

The Avatar starts with their native element and must learn the other three elements by finding masters around the world.

The Avatar can eventually unlock:

- All four elements
- Advanced bending techniques
- Avatar State
- Powerful elemental combinations

The Avatar State should be an extremely powerful temporary transformation that increases bending damage and ability strength.

4. Open World

Create a large, explorable world with four major nations.

Each nation must have:

- Unique architecture
- Different environments
- NPCs with daily routines
- Shops and merchants
- Trainers and bending masters
- Quests and side missions
- Hidden locations
- Enemies and dangerous creatures

The player can travel between nations using boats, air travel, mounts, and other transportation methods.

The world should feel alive, with a day-and-night cycle and changing weather.

5. Player HUD and Interface

Create a clean, beautiful RPG interface.

At the bottom of the screen, display:

Health Bar: Shows the player's current health.

Energy Bar: Represents the player's bending energy. Using bending abilities consumes energy, which regenerates over time.

Inventory: A visible inventory button that opens the player's backpack.

The inventory should contain:

- Weapons
- Clothing
- Food
- Potions
- Materials
- Quest items
- Collectibles

Also include:

- Player level
- Experience bar
- Current bending element
- Map
- Quest tracker
- Ability shortcuts

The HUD should remain visible while exploring and fighting.

6. Combat and Progression

Create real-time combat where the player can combine basic attacks, bending abilities, dodging, blocking, and special moves.

The player earns experience by:

- Defeating enemies
- Completing quests
- Exploring locations
- Training with masters
- Discovering secrets

Leveling up should unlock new abilities and improve the player's bending mastery.

7. NPCs and Interactions

The world must contain interactive NPCs.

Players should be able to:

- Talk to characters
- Accept quests
- Buy and sell items
- Learn bending techniques
- Challenge other benders
- Make friends and enemies
- Discover stories and secrets

NPCs should react to the player's actions and reputation.

8. Important Gameplay Features

- Fully open-world exploration.
- Third-person camera.
- Smooth character movement.
- Running, jumping, swimming and climbing.
- Realistic elemental visual effects.
- Dynamic combat.
- Character customization.
- Inventory and equipment systems.
- Save and load system.
- Main story and optional quests.
- Hidden dungeons and legendary items.
- Unique Avatar-only abilities.

9. Visual Style

Use a beautiful stylized 3D art style inspired by the original Avatar: The Last Airbender animated series.

The environments should be colorful, atmospheric, detailed, and immersive.

Elemental bending should look spectacular, with particles, fluid animations, environmental destruction, and visual effects.

FINAL REQUIREMENT

The result must be a functional, playable game, not just a static visual demonstration or a concept.

Prioritize creating the actual gameplay systems: movement, open-world exploration, elemental bending, combat, character progression, inventory, health, and energy.

Start by building a playable prototype with one explorable area and working bending mechanics, then progressively expand the world and its features.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a playable browser-based 3D RPG prototype inspired by Avatar: The Last Airbender, centered on exploration, bending combat, and progression.
- Deliver a working prototype with one explorable area and responsive controls.

## Requirements
- Build directly without clarification; prioritize playable interactions over a static mockup.
- Keep non-Avatar characters tied to their native element; the larger four-nation world is outside prototype scope.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js and set the prototype in the Southern Reach, with four selectable nation origins and a small chance of Avatar origin.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the origin screen, coastal village and shrine, movement/camera/jump, bending abilities, enemies, NPCs, quest interactions, XP/leveling, inventory/map overlays, and local save/load.
- Fixed quest progression: collecting the relic advances to stage 2, Master Nima offers Healing flow at stage 2, and learning it advances to stage 3.
- Fixed healing to check `health` rather than nonexistent `player.hp`.
- Added `restoreQuestState()` in `game.js` to restore the quest journal, hide a collected relic, and restore the Water Healing flow ability on load.
- Verified relic-return dialogue, Healing flow training, restored quest-stage-3 journal/HUD, and `node --check game.js`; browser console reported no errors or warnings.

### Active
- Finish testing Healing flow activation, enemy combat, and save/load restoration; refresh the gameplay screenshot if needed.

### Blocked
- Browser canvas click was intercepted by `#center-reticle`, preventing bending activation through the attempted canvas click.

## Next Move
1. Test Healing flow and bending combat using a browser interaction that reaches the game canvas.
2. Verify enemy damage/defeat and save/load restoration, then rerun syntax and browser-console checks.
3. Inspect and refresh `screenshots/avatar-gameplay.jpg` if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, controls, combat, NPC dialogue, quest progression, and save/load.
- `index.html`: Game UI, origin screen, HUD, overlays, dialogue, and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual styles.
- `screenshots/avatar-gameplay.jpg`: Gameplay capture; may predate the latest quest-state fix.
- `screenshots/avatar-opening.jpg`: Opening-screen capture.

## Important Context
- Development server: `http://localhost:3002`.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously showed untracked project files including `game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- Browser test save was set to `four-elements-save` with `Kaya`, `questStage: 3`, `health: 60`, and `energy: 80`; starting the game restored the stage-3 journal and health.

Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies

  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs

  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern

## Objective
- Build a playable browser-based 3D RPG prototype inspired by Avatar: The Last Airbender, focused on exploration, bending combat, and progression.
- Deliver one explorable area with responsive controls.

## Requirements
- Build directly without clarification; prioritize playable interactions over a static mockup.
- Keep non-Avatar characters tied to their native element; the larger four-nation world is outside prototype scope.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js and set the prototype in the Southern Reach, with four selectable nation origins and a small chance of Avatar origin.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the origin screen, coastal village and shrine, movement/camera/jump, bending abilities, enemies, NPCs, quest interactions, XP/leveling, inventory/map overlays, and local save/load.
- Fixed quest progression, healing health checks, and `restoreQuestState()` for quest journal, relic visibility, and Water Healing flow ability restoration.
- Fixed canvas clicks being intercepted by `#center-reticle` using `pointer-events:none` in `style.css`.
- Verified bending attacks: enemies register hits, are defeated after three hits, grant XP and silver, and console reports no errors or warnings.

- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Refresh `screenshots/avatar-gameplay.jpg` if needed; no `screenshots/` files were found in the repository.

- (none)

2. Continue any remaining gameplay or presentation polish.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, controls, combat, NPC dialogue, quest progression, and save/load.
- `index.html`: Game UI, origin screen, HUD, overlays, dialogue, and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual styles, including the reticle pointer-events fix.
- `screenshots/`: Expected screenshot location; directory currently absent.

## Important Context
- Development server: `http://localhost:3002`.
